author: Times News
description:
“This is a fundamental issue that I think has got to be addressed in so many ways, because it gnaws away at our confidence in public life.”

In the wake of major antisocial incidents in Birmingham and South London, many across the retail sector have called for more powers to protect staff from crime and intimidation which damage public trust in policing, says former Met Police deputy commissioner Andy Trotter.

Andy Trotter was speaking to Ayesha Hazarika and John Prendergast on Times Radio Drive. Listen every Saturday and Sunday from 4-7pm.

author: Times News
description:
“It’s a very risky, knife-edge moment. I still can’t see the way forward precisely from here.”

Ahead of a potential UN Security Council vote on defensive measures to clear transit through the Strait of Hormuz, President Trump’s increasingly unpredictable behaviour brings the conflict to a ‘hinge-point’, says foreign affairs analyst Sir Robin Niblett.

Sir Robin Niblett was speaking to Ayesha Hazarika on Times Radio Drive. Listen every Saturday and Sunday from 4-7pm.

description:
“The fact that thousands of aircraft have been able to fly without any incidents over the last month of operations is really an amazing feat.”

The hunt is on for the US pilot shot down over Iran, with the chances of survival coming up against the risk of being captured, says retired US Air Force brigadier-general Houston Cantwell.

description:
“If the Iranians do have a hostage in custody, it makes it a lot harder to pull away, declare victory, and take an off-ramp.”

Trump may find himself in a situation similar to Israel’s if Iran holds the missing pilot hostage, says Director of Analysis at Eurasia Group, Marc Gustafson.

description:
"One has to ask the question whether the man did not surive the crash or whether he's out here somewhere."

The United States will be doing “everything they can” to find the airman, but what is “worrying” is that his tracking device may not be working, says former head of the British Army, Lord Dannatt.

Lord Dannatt was speaking to Peter Cardwell and Kate Gerbeau on Times Radio Breakfast. Listen live every Friday to Sunday from 6–10am.

description:
“If they are captured and then paraded in front of the television, that is a huge propaganda tool.”

It is “really important” the stranded US serviceman is returned because their capture “would probably change the course of the war”, says defence analyst and former air Vice-Marshal Sean Bell.

Sean Bell was speaking to Kate Gerbeau and Peter Cardwell on Times Radio Breakfast.
